Let
\[
D=c^2+4ab,\qquad L=2bx+2ay+ct,
\]
and
\[
M=2z(cH+2bE+2aF+xy+yx)+zt^2+2aq^2-2bp^2+c(pq+qp).
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[z,D,L,M].}
\]

Here is the verification.

The element \(z\) is central by assumption. Since \(a,b,c\) commute with one another and with \(p,q,x,y,t,z\), and transform as the adjoint \(sl_2\)-triple
\[
[H,a]=2a,\quad [H,b]=-2b,\quad [E,b]=c,\quad [E,c]=-2a,\quad [F,a]=-c,\quad [F,c]=2b,
\]
we have
\[
[E,D]=2c[E,c]+4a[E,b]=-4ac+4ac=0,
\]
and similarly \([F,D]=[H,D]=0\). Thus \(D\in Z(R)\).

For
\[
L=2bx+2ay+ct,
\]
one checks
\[
[H,L]=0,\quad [E,L]=2cx+2at-2at-2cx=0,\quad [F,L]=0.
\]
Also
\[
[L,x]=2a[y,x]+c[t,x]=-2ac+2ac=0,
\]
\[
[L,y]=2b[x,y]+c[t,y]=2bc-2bc=0,
\]
\[
[L,t]=2b[x,t]+2a[y,t]=-4ab+4ab=0.
\]
So \(L\) commutes with every generator, hence \(L\in Z(R)\).

Now set
\[
T=cH+2bE+2aF,\qquad N=xy+yx+\frac12t^2.
\]
A direct commutator calculation gives
\[
[T,p]=cp+2aq,\qquad [T,q]=-cq+2bp,
\]
and
\[
[T,x]=2cx-2at,\quad [T,y]=-2cy+2bt,\quad [T,t]=-4bx+4ay.
\]
Meanwhile
\[
[N,x]=-2cx+2at,\quad [N,y]=2cy-2bt,\quad [N,t]=4bx-4ay.
\]
Thus \(T+N\) commutes with \(x,y,t\). The \(p,q\)-part is cancelled by
\[
P=2aq^2-2bp^2+c(pq+qp),
\]
because using \([p,q]=z\),
\[
[P,p]=-2z(cp+2aq),\qquad [P,q]=2z(cq-2bp).
\]
Therefore
\[
M=2z(T+N)+P
\]
commutes with \(p,q,x,y,t\). The same adjoint-invariance check as above shows \(M\) commutes with \(E,F,H\), and it plainly commutes with \(a,b,c,z\). Hence \(M\in Z(R)\).

It remains to see that there are no other central elements. Give \(R\) the PBW filtration. Its associated graded algebra is the symmetric algebra on the same generators, with Poisson bracket induced by the displayed commutators. If \(C\in Z(R)\), then its leading symbol \(\sigma(C)\) lies in the Poisson center.

Solving the corresponding first-order Poisson equations gives exactly
\[
\operatorname{PZ}(\operatorname{gr}R)
=
k[z,\ c^2+4ab,\ 2bx+2ay+ct,\ \sigma(M)].
\]
Indeed, the equations from \(p,q,x,y,t,a,b,c,E,F,H\) force every Poisson-central polynomial to be independent of all directions except the four invariant combinations above. Since \(z,D,L,M\) are genuine central lifts of those four algebraically independent leading symbols, subtracting the matching polynomial in \(z,D,L,M\) lowers the PBW degree. Induction on degree then shows every central element lies in \(k[z,D,L,M]\).

Therefore
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k\!\left[z,\ c^2+4ab,\ 2bx+2ay+ct,\ 2z(cH+2bE+2aF+xy+yx)+zt^2+2aq^2-2bp^2+c(pq+qp)\right]}.
\]
